ICYMI: Interview with Mary Houlihan
On the latest podcast
episode
, Mary Houlihan, a comedian, discussed her humorous approach to independent reporting. In addition, she talked about her reporting on detention centers.
The episode is available on
Apple Podcasts
.
Can Journalism Be Funny? ft. Mary Houlihan
Podcast Episode · The Study Hall Podcast · October 19 · 33m
Apple Podcasts
The listings are now posted throughout the week on our
Opportunity Finder
.
If you have any technical questions or want to submit an opportunity m, please email ‘
support AT studyhall DOT xyz
with “Opps:” in the subject line.
Please note:
Anything marked as “
NEW
” is from the past seven days and is included alongside newly added opps (but more than one week old). Finally, old opps from previous issues with upcoming deadlines are listed at the end of the newsletter.
OTHER RESOURCES
▶ Add to the Rate-Sharing Database
The
Freelance Solidarity Project
maintains an ongoing
Rate Sharing Database
to build a clearer picture of freelance pay—and, ultimately, change how we are paid. Add your rates, and help build a more equitable future for freelancers in the industry.
The latest party in the Deez Drinks event series is
"The Publishing Party,"
bringing together everyone in New York's publishing industry and book biz together under one roof for a night (and with an open bar) on Oct. 27. All literary-minded folks are welcome,
tickets
are $20.
Writers Sarah Miller and A.S. Hamrah are teaching a two-day (in person and on Zoom from November 14 and 15t)
writing class
about using “humor as a weapon.” The class will show you how to “get comfortable with strong feelings and opinions required for memorable writing” and “understand how to make things you think are funny funny to others.” More info
here
.
The Institute for Independent Journalists have opened registration for the
Fall 2026 Business of Freelancing course
, offered from Oct. 1 through Nov. 19.
This eight-week, live online course provides a comprehensive foundation in the business of freelance journalism and has sold out every time they’ve presented it. Each session combines real-world strategy with personalized guidance, covering topics such as rate setting, time and income management, client relationships, and long-term planning.
Registration is $249 before Sept 24, and $299 after.
They’ve also announced
their lineup of webinars
for freelancers, featuring assigning editors, fellowship directors, and independent creators. Each webinar runs from 12-1:15 pm EST and costs $30.
Nov. 20 Fund your Freelancing with Fellowships and Grants
Dec. 11 Pitching Arts, Culture, and Travel Stories
Jan. 22 Winning Revenue Strategies for Creator Journalists
Feb. 4-5 Pitch the Editors: Sign Up for 1:1 Pitch Sessions
Workshops from Press On:
The Business of Freelancing
with Lisa Armstrong, Press On board member on Thursday, October 29 @ 1:00-2:15pm ET // 12:00-1:15pm CT // 10:00-11:15am PT.
Register here by October 22nd to save your spot.
Open to all, geared towards independent movement journalists. More details below.
CALLS FOR PITCHES
Please note:
We are not endorsing every publication or company listed here. Engaging with a publication or company is entirely up to the reader. We currently sort each section from the most to least recently posted.
Final note:
Before pitching,
always
check the links to confirm the opportunities are still available.
TIME-SENSITIVE PITCH CALLS
-
USA Today Director of Election Results Operations, Kelly Martin, shared with Study Hall that they are hiring Election Night Stringers based in the US to report election results on November 3, 2026. They will upload new results as officials release them and remain on site to answer questions about the release process. Candidates should have availability on election night and the ability to complete a short training prior to election day. The rate is a flat fee of $125. Send an email to
kmartin@usatodayco.com
with your name, phone number, zip code, and a brief statement on why you are a good fit for the role. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Sep 28)
EVERGREEN PITCH CALLS
NEW:
-
Hunker is
hiring
freelance writers for home and garden content, including home maintenance, gardening tips, and DIY decor. They will produce short and long-form assignments, including celebrity interior design tips, product roundups, and cleaning hacks. Candidates should have a passion for home and garden topics and the ability to produce original, well-researched content. The rate is $21 to $25 per hour or $0.08 to $0.10 per word. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 21)
NEW:
-
The California Post, a New York Post spinoff based in LA, is looking for pitches on culture, lifestyle, and trends across California. They are seeking 750-word pieces with strong takes on home, dating, arts and culture, and California-focused national trends that adopt the punchy, sardonic voice of the Post.The rate is $400 per published column. Send pitches to
hblackman.consultant@californiapost.com
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 20)
-Gendrics is
accepting submissions
of “thoughtful, original contributions about mental health, psychology, emotional wellbeing, gender, and related research.” They welcome submissions from psychologists, mental health professionals, researchers, university faculty, and writers with relevant knowledge or experience. “We prioritize submissions that fit our editorial focus and offer clear value to readers.” The rate is not given, but they “welcome submissions from qualified professionals, researchers, academics, students, and writers with relevant knowledge or experience.” Send pitches to
publisher@gendrics.com
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 15)
-
Dazed is
calling for
story and photography pitches from US-based Gen Z creators for "State of Youth," an editorial series exploring underground subcultures and underrepresented communities. They are seeking distinctly American stories and photo essays highlighting local youth scenes across US states and territories from writers and photographers who have not yet had a major byline. The rate is $300 per published piece. Send pitches through the
Dazed Club app
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 14)
-
TechEngage is always
looking for pitches
of “practical, actionable, and verifiable” tech content, including “explainers and guides on consumer technology, apps and software, AI, cybersecurity, startups and practical tools.” They also accept “analysis and opinion with a clear argument, evidence readers can evaluate, and disclosed conflicts of interest.” The rate is $100 per article. Send pitches to
team@techengage.com
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 14)
-
Queer & Trans Wealth is always
looking for pitches
of personal essays on “how you’re making and saving money in 2025.” They are “especially interested in hearing from trans folks who live in red states — especially if you can’t afford to move, or are deliberately building safe spaces where you live.” The rate is $300 for 700 to 1,000 words. Send pitches to
hello@queerandtranswealth.org
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 14)
-
PQR News is always
looking for pitches
of “clear, accurate explainers and reported pieces that genuinely help readers.” They want “first-hand expertise, careful analysis and reported explainers. We are far less interested in generic listicles, rewritten press releases, or thinly disguised marketing for a product or service.” The salary is arranged case by case. Send pitches through their
contact page
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 14)
-
Jamie Lawrence of Ellipsus shared with Study Hall that they are always looking for essays, deep-dives, and reported pitches on writing, publishing, and creative communities in the age of generative AI. They are seeking thoughtful, personal, and analytical pieces exploring fandom culture, online writing platforms, and how technology and corporate policies affect creative work. The rate is $250 for 700 to 800 words. Send a pitch, writing samples, and a short bio to
social@ellipsus.com
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 14)
FELLOWSHIPS, INTERNSHIPS, AND RESIDENCIES
NEW:
-
The New York Times is
accepting applications
for its A.I. Initiatives Fellowship in NYC, a program combining machine learning and journalism to tackle newsroom investigative challenges. The year-long program is based in NYC and runs from June 2027 to May 2028. Applicants should have no more than five years of professional experience in journalism or machine learning, experience analyzing data and working with LLMs, and prior newsroom editorial experience. The salary is $82,414.80, and this is a guild position.
Apply through the
fellowship page
by November 20.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 23)
NEW:
-
Versant is
hiring
an intern for its MS NOW News & Content Production internship in NYC, where they will help shape a news brand that commands one of the most engaged audiences on television and reaches millions of Americans across cable, online, social media, and audio platforms every day. Interns may be placed in areas such as newsgathering, digital and audio, social media, content strategy, dayside and weekend production, primetime, and production operations. Candidates must be enrolled in a degree-granting program during the internship period, be available to work 40 hours per week on-site, and have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above. The hourly rate is $19.00 to $25.00.
Apply through the
job page
by November 16.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 22)
NEW:
-
The Financial Times is
hiring
an Editorial Engagement and Growth Summer Intern based in NYC to help FT journalism reach a broader audience by producing original content for social media, directly engaging with readers, and managing engagement projects. They will develop ideas for news events and breaking news, assist in social media production, and analyze audience behavior. Candidates should have experience in journalism, design, and video editing, and be authorized to work in the US. The rate is $22 per hour for 40 hours per week, and the internship runs from June 7 to August 13, 2027.
Apply through the
job page
by November 2.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 22)
NEW:
-
Audubon is
accepting applications
for its Editorial Fellowship, a training program for early-career journalists to contribute digital and print reporting on birds, science, and the environment. The six-month program is based in NYC and runs from January to June 2027. Applicants should have reporting and writing experience, an avid interest in wildlife and conservation issues, and graduate coursework in journalism or equivalent experience. The rate is $20 per hour. Apply through the
fellowship page
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 21)
NEW:
-
The Minnesota Star Tribune is
accepting applications
for its Summer Sports Reporting Internship, a program for college juniors, seniors, and graduate students to cover breaking news, live sports, and enterprise stories. The 10-week program is based in Minneapolis, MN and runs from early June to early August. Applicants should have reporting experience, a demonstrated interest in sports, and the ability to work under deadline pressure. The rate is $21.25 per hour.
Apply through the
application page
by November 13.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 20)
-The Argument is
accepting applications
for The Argument Fellowship, a yearlong, full-time program based in Washington, DC to train early-career opinion journalists. Running from January to December 2027, fellows will report and write on a dedicated beat, co-author the Sunday newsletter, produce multimedia content, and participate in editorial workshops. Candidates should have one to two years of professional or academic experience, strong analytical and writing skills, and curiosity about politics, policy, and culture.The salary is $50,000. Send a resume, cover letter, writing samples, references, and two examples of content you appreciated despite disagreeing with them to
jobs@theargumentmag.com
. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 14)
GRANTS, SCHOLARSHIPS, CONTESTS, COURSES, AND PRIZES
NEW:
-Narratively is
accepting applications
for the 2026 Memoir Prize, seeking “revealing and emotional first-person nonfiction narratives from unique and overlooked points of view.” The winner will receive publication on Narratively and participate in a virtual awards ceremony, with author Alexander Chee serving as guest judge. The prize is $3,000.
Apply through the
grant page
by December 6, 2026.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 19)
FULL-TIME JOURNALISM JOBS
NEW YORK CITY
NEW:
-
The Financial Times is
hiring
a US Sports and Leisure Correspondent based in New York to cover the business of sports and consumer brands tied to it. They will produce scoops about deals and investments, write profiles of billionaires and private equity firms, and cover major US sportswear and equipment companies. Candidates should have a proven track record of building contacts, breaking stories, and working well within a team. The salary range is $80,000 to $120,000.
Apply by October 28.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 22)
NEW:
-
The Financial Times is
hiring
a US Legal Correspondent based in New York to cover law and the legal industry, including white collar crime and financial enforcement, and the powerful law firms operating in the US. They will cover federal and New York authorities responsible for investigating and prosecuting financial and corporate malfeasance, develop sources in the criminal defense bar and state and federal courts, and pick out unique angles on New York law firms and prominent lawyers. Candidates should have a proven track record of breaking stories on news-heavy beats and the ability to quickly parse complex legal documents. The salary range is $90,000 to $135,000.
Apply by October 28.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 22)
NEW:
-
MS NOW is
hiring
a Writing Associate Producer based in NYC for its new weekday show, State of Play, airing 11AM - 12PM ET on Monday through Friday with host Peter Alexander. The role involves researching and writing daily segments, editing lower-third banner chyrons, and leading production for digital platforms. Candidates should have three or more years of experience in journalism, strong research skills, and knowledge of American politics and global news. The salary range is $75,000 to $80,000. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 22)
NEW:
-
Fox Weather is
hiring
a Freelance Assignment Editor based in NYC to coordinate real-time weather coverage and breaking news across platforms. They will communicate with sources and affiliates, monitor breaking weather news, pitch segments and guests, and select live visuals and graphics. Candidates should have at least one year of TV newsgathering or assignment desk experience, strong editorial judgment during breaking news, and an understanding of weather science. The rate is $32 to $40 per hour. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 21)
NEW:
-
Literary Hub is
hiring
a Senior Editor based in NYC to help launch and manage a new vertical covering books across all categories. They will develop editorial strategy and workflows, commission and edit reviews and book roundups, oversee weekly newsletters, and manage freelance writers and budgets. Candidates should have at least four years of experience in book publishing and digital media, experience managing staff or freelancers, and deep familiarity with online book culture. The salary range is $72,000 to $75,000.
Send a resume and three pitches for timely book lists to
jobs@lithub.com
by November 6.
See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 21)
NEW:
-
Inc. is
hiring
a Senior Marketing Editor based in NYC to lead and grow the marketing section on
Inc.com
. They will assign and edit daily news and enterprise coverage, manage staff writers and freelance contributors, use performance data to guide editorial strategy, and support live event programming. Candidates should have at least five years of digital editorial experience, proven skill managing writers, and a track record of growing digital audiences. The salary range is $89,000 to $110,000, and this is a guild position. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 20)
NEW:
-
NBC News is
hiring
an Assignment Editor based in NYC for the Network News Desk to coordinate newsgathering and logistical support across broadcast, cable, digital, and streaming platforms. They will research and implement coverage of breaking news, collaborate with digital and broadcast teams, and manage field assignments. Candidates should have three years of editorial production experience and proficiency with newsroom systems and social media. The salary is $70,000 to $85,000. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 20)
NEW:
-
Gizmodo is
hiring
a Head of Social and Video based in NYC to lead video and social strategy, production, and distribution across Gizmodo, Kotaku, and io9. They will develop original video formats, oversee channel strategy across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, manage a team of contributors, and oversee the production budget. Candidates should have at least seven years of social media or video experience, a track record of growing audience engagement, and cultural fluency in tech, gaming, or pop culture. The salary range is $110,000 to $150,000. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 19)
NEW:
-
The Wall Street Journal is
hiring
a Standards Editor based in NYC to uphold reporting standards and ensure fairness and integrity across the newsroom. They will conduct pre-publication reviews of high-impact stories, collaborate with media attorneys to guide reporters, adjudicate editorial disputes, and resolve post-publication issues. Candidates should have at least 10 years of journalism and leadership experience, sharp news judgment, and deep knowledge of Wall Street Journal standards. The salary range is $190,000 to $225,000. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 19)
NEW:
-
The New York Times is
hiring
a FOIA Editor based in NYC to guide newsroom strategy for using public records laws to obtain information from governmental entities. They will advise reporters on integrating records requests into early reporting, propose FOIA-driven story ideas, maintain a central tracking database, and partner with the legal team on litigation. Candidates should have at least five years of journalism or media experience, demonstrated success navigating public records laws, and familiarity with media law. The salary range is $124,979.94 to $150,000, and this is a guild position. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 19)
NEW:
-
MS NOW is
hiring
a Writing Associate Producer based in NYC for The Moment with Katy Tur, a weekday political talk show airing from 2PM - 4PM. They will research and write daily segments, determine video and sound elements, and pitch story ideas. Candidates should have at least two years of journalism experience, strong research skills, and knowledge of American politics and global news. The salary range is $75,000 - $80,000. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 19)
NEW:
-
Fox News Media is
hiring
a Freelance Associate Producer based in NYC to write scripts and help produce daily news broadcasts for The Faulkner Focus. They will write copy and teases, pitch guests and segments, select visual elements, and assist in the control room during breaking news. Candidates should have television news experience, strong knowledge of politics and current events, and the ability to work under tight deadline pressure. The rate is $28 to $36.06 per hour. See our
Opps Finder listing
for more info.
(Oct 19)
-
GQ is
hiring
a Commerce Writer, Lifestyle based in NYC to produce commerce and service journalism across grooming, wellness, fitness, and modern lifestyle. They will write product recommendations, first-person reviews, and evergreen guides, adapt content across newsletters, social media, and short-form video, and apply SEO and analytics to optimize coverage. Candidates should have at least two years of writing experience in a digital media environment, strong knowledge of SEO and commerce data, and comfort creating multiplatform content including video. The salary range is $75,000 to $83,000
